QuestionStmt.S: The solubility product of PbI₂ is $1.08 \times 10^{-7}$. Calculate its solubility in mol dm⁻³ at 298 K.

Solution.S:
The dissociation of PbI₂ is:

$$\mathrm{PbI_2(s) \rightleftharpoons Pb^{2+}(aq) + 2I^-(aq)}$$

Let solubility be $S$ mol dm⁻³. Then:

$$[\mathrm{Pb^{2+}}] = S$$
$$[\mathrm{I^-}] = 2S$$

Solubility product expression:

$$K_{sp} = [\mathrm{Pb^{2+}}][\mathrm{I^-}]^2 = S(2S)^2 = 4S^3$$

Given $K_{sp} = 1.08 \times 10^{-7}$:

$$4S^3 = 1.08 \times 10^{-7}$$
$$S^3 = \frac{1.08 \times 10^{-7}}{4} = 2.7 \times 10^{-8}$$

$$S = \sqrt[3]{2.7 \times 10^{-8}} = 3.0 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{mol dm}^{-3}$$

Thus, the correct option is D: $3.0 \times 10^{-3}$.
